headline: High risk of shared-workspace prompt injection and data leakage; both agents can read/write files and use MCP/network by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and use MCP; next-ai-draw-io processes files and natural-language commands. Their shared filesystem/MCP bridge means content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not proven by sandboxed evidence, but the documented surfaces make injection plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or exchanged files
IF either agent parses file content or diagram text as instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on one side for the shared task
Require explicit human review of any text imported from the other agent
Prefix untrusted content with a non-executable marker convention

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets; next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can call multiple model APIs. A shared workspace can expose sensitive files to both, and the second agent's API-backed processing can move that content off-host. The pairwise leakage path is documented by profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF the same directory contains secrets, source code, or git history
IF next-ai-draw-io sends imported file contents to a remote model API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared directory
Use a scrubbed staging folder for diagrams and PDFs
Route next-ai-draw-io to a local model only
Rotate any credentials present in the workspace after use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has filesystem write, git modification, shell, and subprocess capabilities; next-ai-draw-io can also use files and MCP, so both can mutate the same workspace. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, making concurrent edits and git-state conflicts dangerous by default. Uncertainty about orchestration should be treated conservatively.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or diagram directory
IF either agent writes while the other is editing or committing
mitigations: Assign one agent read-only access
Serialize edits with a simple handoff checklist
Use separate branches per agent
Run git status before and after each agent turn

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code and modify files; next-ai-draw-io can turn inputs into diagrams and other artifacts. If next-ai-draw-io treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The profiles show a plausible handoff but no verification step, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Claude Code output without validation
IF generated text or code is rendered into diagrams or documents
mitigations: Add a human verification step between agents
Require source citations for any factual claims
Limit next-ai-draw-io to formatting-only tasks
Compare outputs against the original source before publishing

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and environment secrets, while next-ai-draw-io can upload content to multiple third-party model providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk for regulated or sensitive data, especially if the shared workspace contains personal or confidential material. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed in files processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF the selected backend is a third-party hosted model without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workspace
Select a local or self-hosted backend
Review retention settings before processing
Document the data flow for the specific deployment
